context.pubinfo_note: From the Consilience cross-theory demo (consilience-demo.netlify.app); its results are pinned in https://github.com/Anuja-Khatri/theconsilience-engine at commit 96ba4e435bd13718d36435cc3436d938d2d1f894, results/demo/. The demo's check rules this disagreement decidable now and names the shared observable both claims bear on; it names no instrument, so none is recorded. This is a statement about the two claims, not a verdict on either theory. The dimension is a dimension of theoretical commitment, not a quantity, so no margin or floor applies. The claim statements in the linked claim cards are reviewed paraphrases with page locators, not quotations.

left.statement: IIT predicts that the duration of a conscious instant is definite and sustained over tens to hundreds of milliseconds, not transient or phasic, as required by the exclusion postulate governing the cause–effect structure of the PSC.
left.direction: “IIT predicts that the duration of a conscious instant is definite and sustained over tens to hundreds of milliseconds, not transient or phasic, as required by the exclusion postulate governing the cause–effect structure of the PSC.” (t003) — expected on shared observables: ignition_signature, temporal_generalization

right.statement: Neural correlates of conscious experience build up gradually across cortical areas, implying a temporal profile for the emergence of conscious content.
right.direction: “Neural correlates of conscious experience build up gradually across cortical areas, implying a temporal profile for the emergence of conscious content.” (c025) — expected on shared observables: ignition_signature, temporal_generalization
